title: Document generation REQ-DCM-012 has no FSD P5 feature section
source: FSD P5 Document hub v3 A1.2 (FEAT-DCM-01 to FEAT-DCM-22), Requirements served row REQ-DCM-012; BRD Program v4 section 5.5 row REQ-DCM-012; BRD Epic 2 v2 section 3.5 rows RWB-E2-017 and RWB-E2-026; TSD P5 Document hub v2 appendix T-A API-P5-016 and API-P5-017; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 16
section: FSD P5 v3 A1.2 feature overview and Requirements served; BRD Epic 2 v2 section 3.5
description: REQ-DCM-012 requires contracts, credit applications and mortgage documents to be generated from approved templates with case data and no re-keying, and the FSD lists it as served in Epic 2. No A2 section, no feature and no acceptance criterion covers generation: the 22 features stop at extraction and the field app. The BRD Epic 2 holds the two stories (RWB-E2-017 screens, RWB-E2-026 engine), the TSD holds the two operations API-P5-016 and API-P5-017, and Architecture v5 slide 16 confirms POST /documents/generate in the P5 contract, so the behaviour is required but has no functional specification in this module.
evidence: FSD P5 v3 Requirements served line: REQ-DCM-012, Must, E2. FSD P5 v3 A1.2: 22 features, none for generation. BRD Epic 2 v2 RWB-E2-017 and RWB-E2-026. TSD P5 v2 T-A.1 API-P5-016 POST /cases/{caseId}/generated-documents and API-P5-017 POST /documents/{documentId}/regenerate. Arch v5 slide 16: REST POST /documents/generate in the P5 IN contract.
proposed: FR-P5-026 and AC-P5-019 carry the behaviour from the BRD Epic 2 requirement and the confirmed v5 operation. The FSD P5 needs a generation section in its next version so that the behaviour has one functional statement.

title: Legal hold REQ-DCM-016 has no FSD feature, the hold API belongs to P3, and the delivery story sits in Epic 8
source: FSD P5 Document hub v3 Requirements served row REQ-DCM-016; BRD Program v4 section 5.5 row REQ-DCM-016 (Must, E1); BRD Epic 1 v4 section 3.5; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1 API sheet (POST /cases/{caseId}/legal-hold owned by P3) and legacy sheet (RWB-AD-021, Epic 8, release 30 June 2027); split_plan.json legacy RWB-AD-021 wave 4; Non Functional Specification v3 NFR-072
section: FSD P5 v3 A1.2 and Requirements served; BRD Epic 1 v4 section 3.5; Ownership Map API and legacy sheets
description: REQ-DCM-016 requires a legal hold to stop deletion and expiry for as long as it is in place, overriding the retention class, and the BRD places it in Epic 1 as a Must. The FSD lists it as served but has no feature and no acceptance criterion. The hold itself is recorded by POST /cases/{caseId}/legal-hold, which the Ownership Map assigns to P3 rwb-case, and the only legacy story that covers hold and retention administration is RWB-AD-021, an Epic 8 story with release 30 June 2027, which the wave map puts in wave 4. A Must requirement in Epic 1 and a wave 4 story cannot both be the delivery position.
evidence: FSD P5 v3 Requirements served: REQ-DCM-016 Must E1; no A2 section. Ownership Map API: POST /cases/{caseId}/legal-hold owner P3. Ownership Map legacy RWB-AD-021: Epic E8, release 30 June 2027, depends on RWB-E1-041. split_plan.json RWB-AD-021: primary P5, wave 4, slices RWB-P5-AD021-CON and RWB-P5-AD021-APP.
proposed: The PRD states the hold as a P5 product behaviour driven by the hold P3 records (FR-P5-025), slices it to wave 4 with RWB-AD-021, and keeps the retention class and the scan in wave 1. The BRD and the story set need one position on the wave.

title: E-discovery and court-ready evidence have no FSD feature, no operation and no response target
source: FSD P5 Document hub v3 Requirements served rows REQ-DCM-017 and REQ-DCM-018; BRD Program v4 section 5.5; BRD Epic 2 v2 section 3.5; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1 API sheet (no discovery operation); Non Functional Specification v3 NFR-073 and NFR-076; TSD P5 Document hub v2 appendix T-A
section: FSD P5 v3 Requirements served; BRD Epic 2 v2 section 3.5; NFS v3 quality characteristics (legal and records)
description: REQ-DCM-017 requires every document of a named population with its metadata, version history and the date each version was created, and REQ-DCM-018 requires a produced document to carry its origin, its entry date, its alteration state and its readers. Neither has a feature, a criterion or an operation: the 17 operations in the TSD and the Ownership Map carry no discovery request, and NFR-073 sets no response time. The behaviour is a Must in Epic 2 in the BRD and cannot be built or accepted from the sources as they stand.
evidence: FSD P5 v3 Requirements served: REQ-DCM-017 and REQ-DCM-018, Must, E2; no A2 section and no acceptance criterion. Ownership Map API sheet: 17 P5 operations, none for discovery or production. NFS v3 NFR-073: response time not set (Open, DL26).
proposed: FR-P5-028, FR-P5-029 and AC-P5-021 carry the behaviour with the response target left open as OQ-P5-09. A discovery operation and its response target are needed before wave 2 acceptance.

title: Sizing, backup and the records management position have no FSD feature and no owned artifact
source: FSD P5 Document hub v3 Requirements served rows REQ-DCM-014, REQ-DCM-015 and REQ-DCM-020; BRD Program v4 section 5.5; BRD Epic 1 v4 section 3.5; Non Functional Specification v3 NFR-071 (Open, DL27) and NFR-069; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 16 and slide 21
section: FSD P5 v3 A1.2 and Requirements served; NFS v3 availability and recovery characteristics
description: REQ-DCM-014 requires storage sized, provisioned and costed for the inbound volume, REQ-DCM-015 a backup on a stated schedule with a restore tested before the first release and at each release, and REQ-DCM-020 a records management position signed by Compliance and Legal. The FSD lists all three as served and gives none of them a feature, a criterion, an owner task or a document. NFR-071 is open under DL27, so even the backup schedule has no value in force.
evidence: FSD P5 v3 Requirements served: REQ-DCM-014, REQ-DCM-015 and REQ-DCM-020, Must, E1; no A2 section. NFS v3 NFR-071: backup on the bank schedule, restore tested, Open, DL27. Arch v5 slide 21: Blob storage with WORM for documents; slide 16: 2.8 TB by 2031.
owner_role: IT lead with the document hub owner
proposed: FR-P5-030, FR-P5-031, AC-P5-022 and AC-P5-023 carry the three obligations as wave 1 release gates, with the schedule and the restore evidence left open as OQ-P5-05.

title: Retention periods are not set while the acceptance criteria assert named retention classes
source: FSD P5 Document hub v3 A2.1.4.2 AC-ALT-P5-001-02, A2.17.4.2 AC-ALT-P5-017-02 and A2.17.4.3 AC-EXC-P5-017-02; Non Functional Specification v3 NFR-028 (Open, DL26); BRD Epic 1 v4 section 7 DL26; TSD P5 Document hub v2 T3.1 retention_action and T3.2 LOV-RETENTION-ACTION
section: FSD P5 v3 A2.17 (retention classes) and A2.1; NFS v3 NFR-028; BRD DL26
description: The acceptance criteria name the retention classes GENERAL05Y and LEGAL10Y, the type-table version DOCTYPE-2026.11 and the retention-table version RET-2026.11 as if they were in force. NFR-028 states that the retention classes are defined per type but the periods are not set, and DL26 is open. The retention rule table itself has no field list in the TSD or the data dictionary. A test can therefore assert a class name without any source of truth for the period behind it.
evidence: FSD P5 v3 AC-ALT-P5-001-02: retention class GENERAL05Y from type table version DOCTYPE-2026.11. AC-ALT-P5-017-02: class GENERAL05Y, version RET-2026.11, expiry. AC-EXC-P5-017-02: class OLD03Y not in RET-2026.11. NFS v3 NFR-028: periods not set, Open, DL26.
proposed: The PRD requires a class on every document and a period from the retention table, treats the class names in the criteria as examples of a reference-table version, and carries the periods as OQ-P5-10. The retention rule field list and the approved periods are needed before wave 1 acceptance.

title: The six document types are counted at 26 fields but only two types name their fields
source: FSD P5 Document hub v3 A2.3.4.1 AC-P5-003-01 and A2.3.4.2 AC-ALT-P5-003-01; BRD Epic 1 v4 section 3.5 RWB-E1-025; BRD Program v4 section 9 DL19; TSD P5 Document hub v2 T3.1 document_type field_definitions
section: FSD P5 v3 A2.3 (document types and their fields); BRD DL19
description: The load criterion asserts the six types and their 26 fields with the Legal and NPA sign-off, and the approval criterion names the fields of two types only: court notice holds court_name, black_case_no, notice_date and hearing_date, and appraisal report holds four fields. The remaining four types and their fields are not enumerated anywhere, and DL19, which fixes which types and fields the hub classifies and extracts, is still open. The extraction build and its evaluation pass marks depend on the full list.
evidence: FSD P5 v3 AC-P5-003-01: the six types and their 26 fields in load file DOCTYPE-2026.11. AC-ALT-P5-003-01: COURT_NOTICE fields court_name, black_case_no, notice_date, hearing_date; APPRAISAL_REPORT 4 fields. BRD Program v4 DL19: which document types and fields, owner Business lead with Legal, due 6 Nov.
owner_role: Business lead with Legal counsel and the Head of NPA
proposed: FR-P5-011 and FR-P5-016 require the full field list to be delivered as the signed reference load and this PRD requires the count to reconcile, not a specific list. OQ-P5-01 and OQ-P5-14 carry the question.

title: The OCR, classification and extraction services are named as external pieces but no source names them or their owner
source: FSD P5 Document hub v3 A2.7, A2.8 and A2.9 (the OCR service, the classifier, the extractor, the scanning service) and their exception criteria; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 16 (TMP Agent: child classify / extract run); TSD P5 Document hub v2 T2 component design; Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 L3 workflow kit
section: FSD P5 v3 A2.7.2, A2.8.2, A2.9.2 and A2.18.2 integration points; Architecture v5 slide 16
description: The FSD treats OCR, document classification, field extraction and malware scanning as external services with versions (OCR engine, classifier version, extractor version) and failure modes (503, no answer in 60 seconds), and the acceptance criteria depend on those failures. No source names the provider of any of the three, its owner, its contract, its endpoint or its version scheme; Architecture v5 names only a child agent run for classify and extract, and the decision record is required to carry the versions (NFR-033, NFR-078).
evidence: FSD P5 v3 A2.7 integration points: the Workbench document hub; A2.8: the Workbench document hub; A2.9: the Workbench document hub; A2.18 integration points: Blob storage. AC-EXC-P5-007-02 (OCR stub returns 503), AC-EXC-P5-008-01 (classifier silent 60 s), AC-EXC-P5-009-02 (extractor silent 60 s). Arch v5 slide 16: TMP Agent child classify / extract run. No owner named in the Ownership Map.
owner_role: Solution architect with the AI product owner
proposed: The PRD keeps the pipeline behaviour in P5 and states the OCR, classification and extraction engines as an external contract reached as an AgentRunCompleted event or a Temporal child run, with the provider, the contract and the version scheme carried as OQ-P5-06.

title: FSD P5 takes branch, mailroom, SFTP and mailbox files inside P5 while Architecture v5 gives P5 no file interface
source: FSD P5 Document hub v3 A2.13, A2.14 and A2.15 (scanner folders, SFTP inbound subfolders, recovery mailboxes) and AC-P5-013-01, AC-ALT-P5-013-01 and AC-ALT-P5-013-02; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 16 (P5 IN contract) and slide 17; Template and Rules v1 DP-16; Microservice Ownership Map v1 API sheet
section: FSD P5 v3 A2.13.3, A2.14.3 and A2.15.3; Architecture v5 slide 16
description: The FSD describes P5 reading a branch scanner folder, polling partner SFTP subfolders keyed by partner code and reading recovery mailboxes, with the channel code, the partner id and the sender address recorded. Architecture v5 slide 16 gives the P5 IN contract REST, the AgentRunCompleted event and the intake workflow only, with no file channel, and DP-16 and the P2 contract make rwb-integration the owner of file exchange. A P5 SFTP client and a P2 file contract cannot both be the intake path.
evidence: FSD P5 v3 AC-P5-013-01: file in the scanner folder of branch BR-0123. AC-ALT-P5-013-01: SFTP inbound subfolder LF-007. AC-ALT-P5-013-02: mailbox MBX-RECOVERY-01. Arch v5 slide 16 P5 IN: REST POST /documents, GET /documents/{id}, GET /cases/{id}/documents, POST /documents/generate; EVT AgentRunCompleted; TMP DocumentIntakeWorkflow. No FILE line in P5 IN. Template and Rules v1 DP-16: recovery.integration.adapter becomes the rwb-integration contract.
proposed: Architecture v5 wins under R-PREC rule 1. rwb-integration takes the file from the channel and hands it to P5 as an intake item; P5 keeps the source, the channel, the capture time, the hash and the duplicate rule, and records no file-system path of its own. The FSD intake sections need the same correction.

title: The TSD extends the ACE Attachment object while the requirement makes the hub the system of record in Blob with WORM
source: TSD P5 Document hub v2 T3.1 (document, EXTEND ACE Attachment) and T3.3 (document to party); FSD P5 Document hub v3 A2.19 and Requirements served REQ-DCM-002; BRD Program v4 section 5.5 REQ-DCM-002; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 8, 16 and 21 (Blob with WORM, rwb-document only)
section: TSD P5 v2 T3.1 and T3.3; FSD P5 v3 A2.19; Architecture v5 slides 16 and 21
description: The TSD declares the document table an extension of the ACE Attachment object and gives it a relationship to the ACE party, which is the monolith position in which the authoritative copy sits in ACE. REQ-DCM-002, DT06, FSD A2.19 and Architecture v5 make the Workbench document hub the system of record, with the file in Blob with WORM written by rwb-document only, and the service may hold no grant on an ACE table under ADR-010 and DP-01.
evidence: TSD P5 v2 T3.1: document (EXTEND ACE Attachment); T3.3: document party_id to party. FSD P5 v3 A2.19: the document is written to the Workbench document hub as the record. Arch v5 slide 21: Blob storage with WORM: documents (rwb-document only). Slide 16: DB writes schema rwb_document; FILE Azure Blob (WORM).
proposed: The PRD states the hub as the record with the file in Blob and the metadata in `rwb_document`, and reads the ACE Attachment extension as the legacy position to be dropped in the next TSD version. OQ-P5-12 carries the confirmation.

title: Signatures are owned by P5 in Architecture v5 and the Ownership Map but have no requirement, feature or story
source: Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 41 (P5 owns metadata, custody, OCR text and fields, signatures, retention) and slide 16 (rwb_document: signatures); Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1 tables sheet (signature_request, owner P5); FSD P5 Document hub v3 A1.1 scope and A2.1 to A2.22; BRD Epic 2 v2 section 3.5 RWB-E2-018
section: Architecture v5 slides 16 and 41; Ownership Map tables sheet; FSD P5 v3 A1.1
description: Architecture v5 puts signatures in the P5 schema and the Ownership Map assigns the signature_request table to P5, but the FSD scope is store, index, OCR, classification, extraction, review queue, retention and custody, with no signature feature, requirement or criterion, and the e-signature flow of Epic 2 is split across P6, P5 and S2. The service therefore owns a table and a contract term with no product behaviour behind them.
evidence: Arch v5 slide 41: P5 rwb-document owns metadata, custody, OCR text and fields, signatures, retention. Ownership Map tables: signature_request owner P5. FSD P5 v3 A1.1 in scope: store, index, OCR, classification, extraction, review queue, retention, custody. No signature section in A2.1 to A2.22. BRD Epic 2 RWB-E2-018: e-signature flow, split P6, P5, S2.
owner_role: Solution architect with P6 and S2
proposed: The PRD records the signature request as a document event and a metadata row on the document, keeps the signing journey with P6 and S2, and carries the missing requirement text as OQ-P5-13.

title: The FSD makes document intake a 15-minute scheduled job while Architecture v5 makes it an event-started workflow with KEDA workers
source: FSD P5 Document hub v3 AC-BG-P5-001-01 to AC-BG-P5-022-01 (document intake, schedule, every 15 minutes), A2.7 and A2.17 (JOB-12, JOB-17); Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 16 and 44; Microservice Ownership Map v1 jobs and workflows sheets; Template and Rules v1 DP-10
section: FSD P5 v3 system background events and A2.7, A2.17; Architecture v5 slides 16 and 44
description: Every one of the 22 background-event tables gives document intake as a schedule that runs every 15 minutes, and the retention feature runs JOB-17 as a monthly job. Architecture v5 slide 44 gives JOB-12 as an event plus KEDA workers and JOB-17 as a Schedule in rwb-document (monthly, 1st Sunday), and slide 16 makes intake a DocumentIntakeWorkflow on queue rwb-document. The Ownership Map replacement for JOB-12 is an event-started workflow, so the two mechanism statements disagree.
evidence: FSD P5 v3 AC-BG-P5-001-01 to AC-BG-P5-022-01: document intake, schedule, every 15 minutes. Arch v5 slide 44: JOB-12 owner rwb-document, mechanism event plus KEDA workers; JOB-17 owner rwb-document, Schedule, monthly 1st Sunday. Slide 16: TMP DocumentIntakeWorkflow, Schedule: retention. Ownership Map jobs: JOB-12 replacement event-started workflow, JOB-17 replacement Temporal Schedule.
proposed: Architecture v5 wins. The PRD states intake as an event-started DocumentIntakeWorkflow with KEDA workers on queue rwb-document, keeps the 15-minute cadence as a schedule that raises the intake, and states JOB-17 as a Temporal Schedule on the 1st Sunday of the month.

title: NFR-042 still requires logging the data lake copy of the document store although the data lake is removed
source: Non Functional Specification v3 NFR-042; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 7, 8, 37 and 44; Template and Rules v1 DP-17 and ADR-018; BRD Program v4 section 6
section: NFS v3 privacy and access characteristics (NFR-042); Architecture v5 slides 7 and 8
description: NFR-042 requires every read of the case store, the document store and the data lake copy to be logged. Architecture v5 states that the Workbench never connects to the data lake, that INT-19 and INT-20 are removed and that reporting reads events into rwb-reporting, and DP-17 removes the lake. There is no lake copy of the document store to log, so the requirement names a store that does not exist in the target.
evidence: NFS v3 NFR-042: every read of the case store, the document store and the data lake copy is logged. Arch v5 slide 8: no data lake or Power BI connection, INT-19 and INT-20 removed. Slide 37 and DP-17: reporting from events into rwb-reporting.
proposed: The PRD requires every read of a document and of its extracted fields to be logged and carries no lake clause. NFR-042 needs the same correction in its next version.

title: The BRDs carry no status field and no approval record, so the requirements approval gate has no recorded baseline
source: BRD Program v4 document control table; BRD Epic 1 v4 document control table; BRD Epic 2 v2 document control table; Template and Rules v1 section R1 U8
section: Document control of the three BRDs
description: None of the three BRDs this PRD reads carries a status field, a decision row or an approval row in its document control table, and no governance record for a Product Owner decision is present in the source set. The requirements approval gate therefore has no recorded baseline, although the requirement tables are complete and versioned.
evidence: BRD Program v4 document control: Document, Version, Date, Classification, Owner rows; no Status row and no approval table. BRD Epic 1 v4 and Epic 2 v2: the same. Template and Rules v1 U8: no human verification stop in this run.
proposed: The PRD is issued as Draft with an empty approval table and the gate stays open. The BRD next versions add a Status row and the Product Owner decision.

title: Two FSD features assert the same review-queue criteria and the correction feed has no distinct criterion
source: FSD P5 Document hub v3 A2.10 (FEAT-DCM-10) and A2.11 (FEAT-DCM-11) with AC-P5-010-01 to AC-EXC-P5-010-08 and AC-P5-011-01 to AC-EXC-P5-011-08; BRD Epic 1 v4 RWB-E1-054
section: FSD P5 v3 A2.10.4 and A2.11.4
description: A2.10 routes a low-confidence extraction to the review queue and A2.11 lets a person check it, but both feature sections assert the same eight exception criteria and the same two alternate criteria word for word, and neither states what the correction feeds. RWB-E1-054 requires the correction to be fed back to the labelled set, which no criterion of either section asserts.
evidence: FSD P5 v3 AC-P5-010-01 identical to AC-P5-011-01; AC-EXC-P5-010-01 to -08 identical to AC-EXC-P5-011-01 to -08. BRD Epic 1 v4 RWB-E1-054: the correction is fed back to the labelled set.
proposed: The PRD reads the two sections as one behaviour (queue plus correction) delivered by CAP-P5-010 and FR-P5-017, FR-P5-018, and adds the correction feed in the decision record. The FSD needs one distinct criterion for the feed.

title: The FSD identifies the customer on a document by the ACE person key and the TSD by party id
source: FSD P5 Document hub v3 change note and A2.3.3.2 field catalog (document.person_key, varchar(255), business key, no foreign key); TSD P5 Document hub v2 T3.1 (DF-DOC-003 party_id) and T3.3 (document to party); Recovery Workbench Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8
section: FSD P5 v3 A2.3.3.2 field catalog; TSD P5 v2 T3.1 and T3.3
description: The FSD v3 change note states that document.party_id becomes the business key document.person_key under D-RCV-35 and ADR-010, and its field catalog gives person_key as a varchar(255) with no foreign key. The TSD P5 v2 still carries DF-DOC-003 party_id of type uuid with a relationship to the ACE party table. Under R-PREC the TSD ranks above the FSD, yet the TSD value is the position the FSD explicitly replaced, and a relationship to an ACE table is forbidden by DP-01.
evidence: FSD P5 v3 change note: document.party_id becomes the business key document.person_key. A2.3.3.2: document.person_key varchar(255), the ACE customer this record belongs to (v_ace_customer.person_key), business key, no foreign key. TSD P5 v2 DF-DOC-003: party_id CROSS_REF uuid; T3.3: document party_id to party.
proposed: The PRD takes person_key as the business key of varchar(255) with no foreign key, because the FSD change is the later intent and a foreign key into ACE is forbidden. OQ-P5-14 carries the confirmation and the TSD needs the same correction.
